additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

info.persona: Roy Bernal balances meticulous technical expertise with artistic wanderlust, they wrestle with anxiety‑fuelled perfectionism, spontaneous sketch‑sprees, and a relentless quest for cultural depth.
info.professional_persona: Roy Bernal, a bilingual technical translator and localization specialist, they leverage their disciplined organization and curiosity to manage complex scientific translation projects with precision using CAT tools, translation memory, and rigorous quality assurance while striving toward a senior management role.
info.cultural_background: Born to Mexican immigrant parents and raised in Texas, Roy grew up navigating both Mexican traditions and American suburban life. He celebrates Día de los Muertos and Mexican holidays with his extended family while also embracing Texan community events. His bilingual upbringing fostered a deep respect for cultural nuance, which informs his professional work, and his strong family ties reinforce his collaborative, harmonious approach to relationships.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Roy is an avid art enthusiast who regularly visits regional galleries and enjoys sketching in his notebook. He plays classical guitar, practices mindfulness meditation to manage his worry, and explores the Texas Hill Country through hiking and nature photography. He also loves cooking traditional Mexican dishes, reading contemporary literature in both languages, and volunteering as a bilingual tutor for local youth.
info.sports_persona: Roy Bernal, an avid hill‑country hiker and occasional trail runner, they follow the Texas Rangers and Dallas Cowboys with seasonal enthusiasm, play weekend soccer with the Austin FC fan club, and belong to the Hill Country Hikers group where they meet to explore the Texas scrublands while tracking their steps with a smartwatch.
info.arts_persona: Roy Bernal, a devoted gallery regular and sketch‑book chronicler, they draw inspiration from Frida Kahlo, Edward Hopper, and contemporary photographer Annie Leibovitz while practicing classical guitar pieces by Andrés Segovia and John Williams and devouring novels by Haruki Murakami and Roberto Bolaño in both English and Spanish.
info.travel_persona: Roy Bernal, a meticulous planner who balances family commitments with wanderlust, they have trekked the Texas Hill Country, explored the stone towns of Sedona, savored street food in Mexico City, and toured the art districts of Barcelona, while eyeing future trips to Patagonia’s glaciers and Kyoto’s temples, each itinerary crafted in detailed spreadsheets and guided by off‑peak flight deals.
info.culinary_persona: Roy Bernal, an enthusiastic home chef with a penchant for authentic Mexican cuisine, they expertly prepare mole poblano, chiles en nogada, and slow‑cooked carnitas using dried ancho chilies, epazote, and masa harina, while occasionally experimenting with sous‑vide techniques to perfect the texture of tamales.

info.persona: Marisol Lima balances a methodical professional drive with a love for garden‑fresh flavors, community festivals, and a habit of meticulously planning spreadsheets while occasionally forgetting to water her roses on busy days.
info.professional_persona: Marisol Lima, a seasoned office manager with a business degree, blends meticulous budgeting, bilingual communication, and data‑driven workflow optimization with a curious yet practical mindset, stepping confidently between established protocols and innovative efficiency tools to coach staff and mediate conflicts.
info.cultural_background: Marisol is a Mexican‑American raised in Brownsville, Texas, a city steeped in border culture. She grew up bilingual, celebrating Catholic holidays, Día de los Muertos, and Mexican festivals while also embracing American community traditions. Family ties are central to her identity, and she values collective responsibility, hospitality, and perseverance—traits inherited from her immigrant grandparents. Her cultural background informs her warm interpersonal style, respect for hierarchy, and a pragmatic work ethic that blends traditional values with an openness to new ideas.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Marisol enjoys cooking traditional Mexican and Tex‑Mex cuisine, tending to a modest garden of herbs and roses, and taking daily walks with her dog in the Brownsville park system. She actively participates in community festivals such as Charro Days and Dia de los Muertos, volunteers at a local senior center teaching basic English, and spends quiet evenings reading historical fiction or listening to boleros and mariachi music. Occasionally she paints landscape scenes and travels to Mexico to visit family.
info.sports_persona: Marisol Lima keeps fit by walking her dog through the Brownsville park system five days a week, participates in the local Brownsville Walking Club’s weekend 5 k runs, cheers on the Houston Astros in spring, the Houston Texans in fall, and enjoys occasional pickleball matches at the community center.
info.arts_persona: Marisol Lima enriches her evenings with the melodies of bolero legends like Luis Miguel and the Mariachi Vargas de Tecalitlán, loses herself in historical fiction by Philippa Gregory, and paints tranquil Texas‑Rio Grande landscapes inspired by Claude Monet’s brushwork, while volunteering at Charro Days to showcase traditional dance performances.
info.travel_persona: Marisol Lima prefers purposeful trips that blend family connection and cultural immersion, regularly flying to Oaxaca and Puebla to visit relatives, enjoys weekend getaways to South Padre Island for beach relaxation, and dreams of exploring the historic streets of Seville during the next fall festival season.
info.culinary_persona: Marisol Lima, an accomplished home chef, layers smoky chipotle in homemade enchiladas, slow‑cooks chiles en nogada with freshly harvested cilantro and pomegranate seeds from her garden, and pairs her meals with handcrafted margaritas made from home‑grown lime zest and agave nectar.

info.persona: Marwan Laurinaitis balances a rigorously scheduled routine of meditation, painting, and strategic consulting with a compulsion to collect obscure art monographs, often losing sleep over anxious thoughts yet they find solace in the quiet rhythm of their herb garden.
info.professional_persona: Marwan Laurinaitis, a seasoned strategic advisor and former operations analyst, channels their disciplined analytical rigor and vivid artistic imagination into crafting cross-functional organizational cultures that fuse data-driven decision-making with abstract creative thinking, while they mentor emerging talent through structured yet inspirational workshops.
info.cultural_background: Marwan is a white American whose family lineage blends Lithuanian immigrant roots on his father's side with a Mediterranean (Arabic‑North African) background reflected in his given name. He grew up in the industrial town of Endicott, NY, where a tight‑knit, working‑class community emphasized self‑reliance, order, and modest cultural activities such as community theater and local history societies. His upbringing, coupled with a university education in the arts and humanities, fostered a deep respect for both Western literary canon and the storytelling traditions of his broader ancestry. This hybrid cultural lens informs his appreciation for abstract art, his disciplined work ethic, and his desire to bridge analytical rigor with creative expression.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Marwan spends his free time immersed in solitary creative pursuits such as oil painting on abstract canvases, writing short stories that explore existential themes, and maintaining a detailed sketch journal of his observations in the Finger Lakes region. He also enjoys attending intimate gallery openings, listening to chamber music, and playing chess at the local library. To balance his emotional intensity, he practices mindfulness meditation and tends to a small herb garden, which provides a structured yet calming routine.
info.sports_persona: Marwan Laurinaitis enjoys low-impact fitness through weekly walks along the Seneca Lake shoreline and occasional senior bocce league games at the Endicott Community Center, while they root for the Buffalo Bills and the Rochester Red Wings, and they attend local amateur tennis matches with the Finger Lakes Tennis Club during summer.
info.arts_persona: Marwan Laurinaitis immerses themselves in abstract expressionist canvases by Mark Rothko, attends intimate chamber concerts featuring Yo-Yo Ma, frequents the Corning Museum of Glass, and they contribute thoughtful art criticism to the Endicott Historical Society’s quarterly newsletter, all of which shape their personal creative practice of oil painting and short-story writing.
info.travel_persona: Marwan Laurinaitis favors contemplative road trips to historic art hubs like Florence and Chartres, plans itineraries around museum openings and local culinary markets, but also cherishes annual weekend getaways to the Finger Lakes wine trail, where they unwind among vineyards and the tranquil scenery of Watkins Glen.
info.culinary_persona: Marwan Laurinaitis’s palate leans toward Mediterranean-inspired dishes such as lemon-rosemary grilled sea bass, ratatouille seasoned with fresh basil from their herb garden, and artisanal cheese plates featuring aged Gouda, while they are modest in cooking skill, preferring simple, well-executed recipes over elaborate culinary experiments.
